channel.title: The Tidewater News - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Tidewater News (thetidewaternews.com)

item.title: Calls for county pay increases, schedule changes
item.description: Prominent citizens urge Southampton County supervisors to raise employee pay, adopt twice-monthly paychecks and boost school funding to stay competitive and ease financial strain.

item.title: Family 4 Eternity serves 26K meals ahead of storm
item.description: Family 4 Eternity used a new refrigerated truck to deliver 13,000 pounds of food—about 26,000 meals—to more than 1,000 Western Tidewater residents ahead of Winter Storm Fern.

item.title: COLUMN: You (yes, you!) can help your minister
item.description: A pastor explains why clergy are increasingly hard to replace and offers practical ways church members can support, respect and retain their ministers.

item.title: Cooper: SCPS ’25-’26 Teacher of the Year
item.description: Riverdale Elementary third grade teacher Tynethia Cooper has been named Southampton County Public Schools’ 2025-26 Teacher of the Year after a divisionwide selection process.

item.title: COLUMN: What do public school boards do and how do they do it?
item.description: Bob Holt writes that school board service is far more than a monthly meeting, with effective board members devoting 10-20 hours a week at minimum to management work under Virginia law.

item.title: Deborah Earley Knight
item.description: Deborah Earley Knight, age 83, passed away peacefully on Feb. 7, 2026, surrounded by the love of her family.

item.title: Lions continue to earn success on the court
item.description: Rock Church School varsity boys hoops improves to 14-1 and returns to the top of the MACAA 1A North after big wins over Southampton and rival New Life; JV Lions roll to 9-0.

item.title: 2nd Walk of Love Gathering set for Feb. 28
item.description: Franklin nonprofit The Widow Walk hosts its second free Walk of Love Gathering Feb. 28, offering dinner and speakers for widows and widowers at The Hubs Vine; seating is limited.

item.title: Roy Copeland
item.description: It is with heavy hearts that we announce the passing of our brother, Roy Copeland, who departed this life on Feb. 10, 2026 at home in Windsor, Virginia.

item.title: UPDATED: Council votes to ask Oglesby to return as city manager
item.description: Franklin City Council rejected a contract with Southampton County Administrator Brian Thrower and instead voted 6-1 to ask former city manager Rosylen Oglesby to return.
